summary: Players draft double-sided domino tiles each round based on a value ranking, then place them edge-to-edge into their own personal kingdom, matching terrain types and chasing crown symbols. It's a light, quick, almost meditative spatial puzzle where the only real interaction is competing over which tiles you get to pick, not what happens on anyone's board.
praised: very easy to teach even to kids
satisfying puzzle of shaping a compact kingdom
criticised: low player interaction beyond the draft
can feel too light or repetitive for serious gamers
little to no catch-up mechanism if you fall behind

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with a competitive draft
interaction.detail: The only shared resource is the row of available dominoes each round, where picking a strong tile bumps you later in the next turn order; beyond that, each player builds and scores their own separate kingdom grid with no way to affect anyone else's board directly.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Every point comes from the same formula — the size of each connected kingdom region multiplied by its crown count — so the whole game reduces to one scoring category applied region by region.
scoring.how_you_win: Draft dominoes and place them to build connected same-terrain regions containing crowns; at the end, multiply each region's tile count by its crowns and sum everything, and the highest total wins.
